First problem: In a predicate of XPATH, literals need to be enclosed in quotes. If it is a bug we need to fix it. Second: Online supports jsp expression syntax for attribute values. This means that the value needs to be specified as a java expression enclosed by <%= and %>. If we want offline syntax to be confirming to online syntax, then OCA needs to support jsp expression syntax. Supporting a general expression syntax would require implementation of a java expression evaluator. I do not think that we have the time or a business case for this. If we restrict ourselves to support string concatenation where the strings inside the expression are either literals or getField it is sufficient. This also has an implication that we stick to JSP quoting and escaping sequence while specifying a attribute value. This syntax is not compatable with kXML parser. I would like to punt this to post 4.0. cheers --prasad
